phase1_leaf_result.tested_scope: Self-local deterministic replay of an already accepted single effect and an accepted batch under two concurrent consumers plus crash recovery. Compared (A) a same-authoritative-path consumed state under the existing non-reusable epoch/CAS model and (B) a separately fenced per-effect idempotency record. Covered concurrent consumer claim, crash before outcome, crash after outcome but before durable consumed receipt, duplicate retry, accepted-not-consumed versus consumed distinction, partial batch consumption, and next-invocation recovery after CAS conflict. No live claim/effect mutation, public-source read, external coordinator, other-worker state, O/downstream input, hosted compute, quota-bearing service, or destructive cleanup was used.
observations: For both compared architectures, two consumers racing from the same authoritative base can be reduced to one durable consumption authorization by path/blob CAS plus a stable effect or batch identity and a non-reusable epoch/fence. The losing consumer has no authorization and must reconstruct on a later invocation rather than retrying in-run.
A durable accepted state and a durable consumed state must remain distinct. Treating acceptance as consumption loses crash-recovery information and can suppress an outcome that was never produced.

Marking consumed before producing a useful outcome gives at-most-once authorization but creates a crash window in which the outcome is lost. Producing the useful outcome before marking consumed creates the opposite crash window: the next consumer cannot know from repository state alone whether retry would duplicate the outcome.

A same-authoritative-path consumed set is sufficient for exactly-once repository-state transition only when the useful outcome itself is atomically represented by that same successful CAS mutation. It is not by itself an exactly-once protocol for an arbitrary separately applied useful outcome.

A separately fenced idempotency record narrows contention and gives a stable per-effect recovery locus, but it has the same crash ambiguity unless the useful outcome target accepts the same stable idempotency key or otherwise exposes a durable replay-safe result identity that can be checked before retry.

For an accepted batch, a single batch-level consumed bit is unsafe when effects can complete independently. Safe recovery requires a stable batch manifest plus per-effect consumption states/receipts; after a crash, the next invocation retries only effects not durably consumed and never reissues already consumed effects.

If a batch promises all-or-none useful outcomes across multiple independently applied targets, repository CAS alone cannot provide atomicity across those targets. The replay can preserve exactly-once authorization and recoverable partial progress, but not transactional all-or-none external side effects without an idempotent or transactional target surface.
A CAS conflict remains non-consumption evidence. Deferring to the next invocation is safe when stable effect/batch identity, non-reusable epoch/fence, and accepted/consumed separation are preserved.
phase1_leaf_result.inference: For the exact replayed scope, the same-path and separate-record designs both solve duplicate consumer authorization under recurring Chat, but neither can guarantee exactly-once arbitrary useful outcomes across the crash-after-outcome-before-receipt window unless the useful outcome is atomically coupled to the authoritative CAS or the target surface supports a stable idempotency/result identity. Therefore the recurring-Chat parity protocol should model consumption as a fenced state machine (accepted -> consumption_claimed -> consumed), use stable effect/batch ids, keep per-effect receipts for batches, and classify non-idempotent uncoupled target actions as an unresolved child rather than claiming parity.
phase1_leaf_result.unresolved_child: Test the crash window against two exact target classes: (1) a repository-internal useful outcome that can be atomically coupled to the authoritative CAS and (2) a separately applied action with and without a stable target-side idempotency/result identity. Determine the minimum generic contract needed to promote consumption from exactly-once authorization to exactly-once useful outcome, including partial-batch recovery, without external hosted coordination or finite quota.
